page: Microsoft Azure D16plds_v5 is an ARM-based virtual machine belonging to the DPLDSv5 server family. It is powered by an Ampere Altra ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 processor operating at 3.0 GHz. The server features 16 dedicated physical cores and 16 vCPUs, meaning there is no hyperthreading, with exactly one thread per core. It is equipped with 32.0 GB of RAM, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB of memory per core. Local storage is bundled, providing 614 GB of capacity, and the instance is Premium Storage capable.

Benchmark data indicates average performance across most multi-core and memory operations. The server achieved a stress-ng multi-core CPU score of 28883.33 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 9656.0. Memory bandwidth is measured at 119.88 GB/sec for large-block read-only operations and 68.21 GB/sec for large-block write operations. However, single-core performance is a notable tradeoff, with Geekbench single-core scoring in the bottom 25% at 1092.0, and single-threaded bzip3 decompression also performing weakly at 8.88 GB/sec. Additionally, small-model LLM text generation is poor, registering at 30.85 tokens/sec.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the D16plds_v5 offers a dense allocation of 16 dedicated ARM cores with a lower memory-to-CPU ratio, making it a resource-efficient choice for scale-out workloads that do not require massive memory footprints. The inclusion of 614 GB of local storage enhances its value for disk-heavy tasks. This server is suited for multi-threaded workloads such as software compilation, static web serving, Redis deployments, and database operations.
description: Microsoft Azure D16plds_v5 is an ARM-based virtual machine from the DPLDSv5 family, featuring 16 dedicated physical cores on an Ampere Altra Neoverse-N1 processor running at 3.0 GHz. It is configured with 32.0 GB of RAM and includes 614 GB of local storage. The server delivers average multi-core performance, as shown by its Geekbench multi-core score of 9656.0 and a stress-ng multi-core score of 28883.33. However, single-core performance represents a tradeoff, with Geekbench single-core and single-threaded bzip3 decompression scoring in the bottom 25%. Lacking GPU acceleration, it is not suited for heavy AI generation, but it performs well in multi-threaded tasks. This instance is best suited for software compilation, static web serving, Redis key-value stores, and database operations where dedicated ARM cores and local storage provide efficient resource density.
